incident-bot: :rotating_light: Severity=P1 alert — GPU OOM during prefill on node gpu-node-7. Container runtime-service-abc restarted by OOM-kill at 2025-11-04T03:07:51Z. Prefill size: ~210k tokens, request_id=0x7f9e. Count=3 restarts in last 8m. Paging @sre-oncall.

sre-oncall: taking it. I'm oncall for the night. pulling logs now.

maria.sre: I see the same in cloudwatch: "killed process pid=1423 oom_reaper invoked" plus lots of CUDA OOM traces. Repro looks tied to long-context sessions from customer_id=acme-enterprise (heavy multi-turn import).

lee.runtime: attaching KV cache metrics — looks like KV cache grew beyond eviction thresholds during prefill, then continuous growth -> fragmentation -> cudaMalloc fails. Also saw repeated "CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY" and a driver reset in dmesg: `NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:00:1f): 79` before the container restarted.

jon.platform: rolling a short mitigation: temporarily mark node gpu-node-7 unschedulable and drain. patching routing to avoid the node pool on the short term. Applying a global route rule to send requests > 65k tokens to small-cpu-fallback and to model-quant-8bit.

maria.sre: please also enable prefill-trimming for the customer workspace (limit primary prefix to 100k tokens) — manual override pushed to runtime config: `runtime.request_limits.max_prefill_tokens=100000` for workspace acme-enterprise.

lee.runtime: quick commands I ran:
```
# mark node cordoned
kubectl cordon gpu-node-7
kubectl drain gpu-node-7 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force
# check container events
kubectl -n serving logs runtime-service-abc --previous | tail -n 200
```
logs show repeating prefill chunk sizes and `cudaMalloc` failures.

incident-bot: Note: Customers served by dedicated-pool-east may experience increased latencies or 502s while routing changes propagate. Impact window estimated ~5-15m.

carmen.cs: ACME reported a spike of 502s and session disconnects starting ~03:04Z. They're seeing failed imports on ~3% of requests. I'll open a support ticket and post a brief note.

sre-oncall: current mitigation plan (applied):
- cordon+drain gpu-node-7 :white_check_mark:
- route long-prefill requests -> quant-8bit variant / cpu-fallback :white_check_mark:
- set per-workspace prefill cap 100k for acme-enterprise :white_check_mark:
- enable aggressive KV-cache eviction (short TTL) on pool: in progress :hourglass_flowing_sand:

lee.runtime: enabling aggressive eviction by toggling `kv_cache.eviction_policy=aggressive` on pool config. Also pushing a runtime guard that rejects a single request if estimated prefill > 150k tokens with a 413-ish error and a descriptive message to encourage client-side trimming.

jon.platform: started scale-up of smaller-model capacity to absorb rerouted traffic (dedicated small-quant nodes). Autoscaler already spun +4 quant nodes. Should finish in ~4m.

maria.sre: monitoring GPU mem free after eviction toggle. Early signal: free memory per GPU rose from 0.6GB to ~6GB on the warmed nodes as old kv entries got evicted. No further immediate restarts in the last 3m.

incident-bot: New events: 2 additional restarts on gpu-node-3 at 03:11Z but both survived after drain. Marking as reduced severity.

carmen.cs: Messaging suggestion for ACME support note: short apology, mention transient GPU OOM during large imports, mitigation applied (routing+trimming), ETA for full resolution: 2-3 hours while we finish node replacements and follow-up tuning. I'll send once ok.

sre-oncall: Agree with message. Please include: workaround (reduce import chunk sizes or use compressed prompts), and note we're not seeing model quality regression for rerouted quant models (we validated on sample prompts).

lee.runtime: follow-up actions (for postmortem):
- add conservative prefill token estimator to router (reject/redirect before hitting runtime)
- add KV-cache size watermark alarms per GPU (already instrumented but need alert thresholds)
- adjust default max_prefill_tokens per workspace to 80k for Hosted tier, 150k for Dedicated with opt-in.
- investigate potential leak in kv-cache accounting for long sessions (heap vs cuda allocation mismatch).

jon.platform: creating an incident ticket in JIRA: INF-2025-1123, assigning to runtime and infra. Will include list of affected customers and timeline.

maria.sre: preparing a short triage note for the oncall handoff in 30m. Key details: root cause likely large prefill -> kv cache growth -> cuda OOM -> container restart. Mitigations applied and holding pattern. No data exfil or security impact.

incident-bot: Handoff reminder: @sre-oncall to @next-oncall in 28m. Use triage checklist template: `#triage/prefill_oom`.

sre-oncall: handing off in 27m. Leaving the following in the thread for next oncall:
- current node health: all problematic nodes cordoned/drained, replacements requested, autoscaler up +4 quant nodes.
- active mitigations: prefill cap for acme-enterprise=100k, global routing for >65k tokens, aggressive KV eviction ON.
- evidence: last crash trace attached to ticket INF-2025-1123.

carmen.cs: I'll follow up with ACME ticket and ping account lead.

lee.runtime: quick note: we've enabled `cuda-mem-trace=1` traces on warm nodes to collect more info if it recurs; dropping verbose logs after 2h to limit noise.

sre-oncall: leaving handoff notes in the oncall doc and tagging the incident in slack channel. If any new OOMs appear, escalate to PagerDuty L2.

incident-bot: Incident status update: mitigated->degraded. Next update scheduled in 20m or sooner if regression. :white_check_mark:
